theorem_title: The original even-n integer-quartic weighted series has its exact infinite sum
formal_statement:
theorem ZetaNine.CoefficientMapSummation.original_integer_quartic_exact_infinite_L (n : ℕ) (hn2 : 2 ≤ n) (hn : Even n)
    (W : ℤ[X]) (hW : W.natDegree ≤ 4) :
    HasSum (actualSeries n (W.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))) (exactL n (W.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))):= by sorry
natural_language_statement: For every even integer $n\ge2$ and integer polynomial $W\in\mathbb Z[X]$ with degree at most4, cast its coefficients to $\mathbb Q$ and form the original actual p9,q1,m=n,d0 weighted rational function. The genuine positive sequence has HasSum to its exact $B+\rho_3\Re\zeta(3)+\rho_5\Re\zeta(5)+\rho_7\Re\zeta(7)+\rho_9\Re\zeta(9)$ linear form. The stronger degree bound is proved from the stated quartic/even-n domain. Integer W is not a claim that every rational local coefficient or full linear form is an integer. General parameters, inverse denominator heights, a small nonzero integer-form sequence, J and irrationality are separate obligations.
